title: api: multipart file input support + tool/file payload limits and content-type validation (openai-compat)
author: Aisha Kapoor
description: Context: The OpenAI-compatibility layer and the /v1/responses and /v1/chat/completions endpoints currently accept JSON bodies and a 'files' array for tool/function-calling. Customers want to upload files via multipart/form-data for large tool inputs (e.g., dataset snippets, attachments). This PR adds multipart parsing, per-file payload limits, striccontent-type validation, and a handful of streaming stability patches to ensure streaming + multipart works consistently. Motivation: • Improve developer ergonomics for tools that need file upload • Protect serving runtime from oversized payloads and non-whitelisted content-types • Ensure OpenAI-compat layer behaves predictably when receiving multipart boundaries and streams Design summary: • Add lightweight multipart/form-data parser in api-gateway with streaming backpressure support (max memory usage ~1MB per part) • Enforce per-file and total request size limits configurable via route config (defaults: per_file=5MB, total=50MB) • Validate content-type of each part against an allowlist; reject unknown/unsafe types with 415 and structured error consistent with OpenAI error formats • Wire multipart support into tools/file handling path so that tool-calling payloads accept files from either JSON-embedded base64 or multipart parts • Update openai-compat middleware to normalize file metadata (filename, content_type, size) and attach to the existing request.files structure • Add end-to-end tests for multipart + streaming where body is proxied to the runtime while respecting KV cache and batching • Streaming stability fixes: handle chunked transfer encoding with multipart boundaries, ensure connection close triggers runtime cancel, fix a race in the streaming frame flusher Checklist: - [x] Add multipart parser and streaming tests - [x] Add per-file and total size limits and config knobs - [x] Add content-type allowlist and error mapping - [x] Update openai-compat normalization and docs - [x] E2E tests for tool/file flow (JSON and multipart) - [x] Update API docs and examples - [x] Add changelog/release note Breaking changes: none expected; invalid requests will be rejected earlier with 400/415 which previously may have been passed downstream Rollback plan: Revert middleware registration and feature flag off (feature flag added: api.multipart_enabled) if regressions observed in canary deployments Related: ENG-1023 (tooling file uploads), ENG-1108 (streaming flakes), pr-18432 (file input handling multipart support — referenced for earlier experiments).
commits: feat(api): add streaming multipart parser with backpressure support
feat(api): enforce per-file and total request size limits (configurable)
chore(openai-compat): normalize file metadata from multipart parts
fix(streaming): handle chunked transfer + boundary splicing edge cases
test(api): add e2e multipart tool/file tests and unit tests for content-type validation
docs: update openai-compat docs and examples for multipart uploads
review_comments: Ben Liu: Left a few nits in multipart_parser.rs — specifically around buffer sizing and an unbounded Vec growth. Suggest using a bounded ring buffer for parts > 1MB.
Aisha Kapoor: Addressed the buffer nits, switched to a smallvec-backed buffer with explicit caps. Added a config knob and documented the memory tradeoffs.
Marina Ortiz: Can we make the default per-file limit 5MB rather than 10MB? This keeps the cost predictable for hosted users. Also request an explicit 415 mapping in the compat layer.
Aisha Kapoor: lowered default per-file to 5MB and added 415 error mapping with structured payload per OpenAI error schema. Updated tests.
Samir Patel: E2E tests look good. I did see a flaky streaming test on first CI run — reran and it passed. Please monitor canary metrics for increased 499/408 after deploy.
Marina Ortiz: Approved after CI green and test stability confirmation.
Ben Liu: Approved; small follow-up suggested to extract allowlist into config file for enterprise ships.
Aisha Kapoor: Follow-up ticket filed (ENG-1157) for enterprise allowlist config extraction.
ci_summary: Initial CI run: failed (flaky streaming test). Reran pipeline; green. Checks: unit tests passed, integration e2e multipart tests passed, lint passed, build passed.
release_notes: Added multipart/form-data support for tool/file uploads on OpenAI-compatible endpoints; per-file and total request size limits (defaults: per_file=5MB, total=50MB); content-type allowlist with 415 errors on invalid types; streaming stability fixes for multipart chunked uploads.
notes: Canary rollout enabled for 24h. Watch metrics: api.multipart_rejected, api.multipart_bytes_total, streaming.disconnect_rate. If any increase in runtime OOMs, rollback feature flag.
security_review: security reviewed content-type allowlist and rejection cases. No secrets logged. Added additional audit logging for file uploads (filename redacted) to S3 audit bucket.
why_this_is_safe: Multipart parser uses streaming decode and caps per-part memory; limits enforced before runtime handoff; feature gated and canary-by-default for the first rollout. OpenAI-compat behavior is preserved for JSON-based files.
